transcription.text: On-site, a supervisor reads a heat number and asks,
So what now?
A number cannot say. An answer can.
Weather station answers in one strip.
Danger in words and in instruction.
Act on the recommended steps.
Need the actions?
You can click View Recommended Steps right in the strip to open them.
Two actions in priority order.
First, pause outdoor work and move crews to shade or rest.
Then, details.
It shows the verdict, a data confidence mark, and the last update, in Saudi time.
The heat card also carries the cycle in force.
30 minutes of work, 10 of rest, water every 15.
Next, station health.
One station is offline, and the page names it.
Readiness reads Not Ready.
Another project, same page.
Three readings are in danger.
Heat index, temperature, and pressure.
The page names each.
Back in the first project, a new gear opens select parameters.
Switches choose which readings are featured.
Reports is new.
Pick a period to see the highest heat index and wind speed.
You can export an Excel file.
The safety limits live in settings.
The page warns that changing anything here changes when work stops, for everyone on the project.
Two limits preview the last 30 days.
Temperature would have stopped work on 8 of those days.
Wind would have stopped it on just 1.
Five bands, green to deep red, each with its own settings for work, rest, and water.
The heat index method is NOAA.
Change history has its own tab here.
None were recorded in the history it read.
Each project switches on only the products it uses.
Here, weather station is active.
Gas and lightning, inactive.
Four new places.
Choose what is featured.
Look back at the heat.
Check what stops working.
See which products are on.
Readings travel over the site's wireless mesh to a gateway, then onto the cloud.
The cloud decodes and stores them.
WayCap serves them here.
Next time the heat number climbs, open weather station, if your project has it.
Read the strip first.
